title: Industrial Cable-Laying Cost Function Across a River and Along Land
originalTopic: Theory and Examples: Applied Function Modeling
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A power plant sits on one bank of a river that is 800 ft wide. A new cable must be laid from the plant to a city located 2 mi (10,560 ft) downstream on the opposite bank. Laying cable costs $180 per foot across the river and $100 per foot along the land. (a) Suppose the cable goes from the plant to a point Q on the opposite bank that is x ft downstream from the point P directly opposite the plant, and then along the bank to the city. Write a function C(x) giving the total cost in terms of x. (b) Evaluate C(x) at representative values of x to determine whether the least expensive location for point Q is less than 2000 ft or greater than 2000 ft from point P.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } C(x) = 180\sqrt{800^2 + x^2} + 100(10560 - x); \quad \text{(b) Less than } 2000\text{ ft from } P

steps.title: Compute the Underwater and Overland Cable Lengths
steps.mathExpression: L_{\text{river}} = \sqrt{800^2 + x^2} = \sqrt{640000 + x^2}\text{ ft}, \qquad L_{\text{land}} = 2(5280) - x = 10560 - x\text{ ft}
steps.explanation: Convert 2 miles to feet: 2 * 5280 = 10,560 ft. The right triangle formed by the 800-ft river width and the x-ft downstream offset PQ has hypotenuse sqrt(800^2 + x^2) ft underwater. The remaining distance along the bank from Q to the city is (10,560 - x) ft.
steps.why: All lengths must be expressed in consistent units (feet) before applying the Pythagorean theorem and unit costs per foot.

steps.title: Formulate the Total Cost Function C(x) for Part (a)
steps.explanation: Multiply the underwater length by $180/ft and the overland length by $100/ft, and add the two costs together for 0 <= x <= 10,560.
steps.why: Total cost is the sum of the underwater cable cost and the overland cable cost.

steps.title: Evaluate a Table of Values for Part (b)
steps.why: Tabulating C(x) across [0, 2500] reveals where the total cost decreases and where it begins to increase.

steps.title: Conclude the Optimal Location of Point Q
steps.explanation: The table shows that C(x) reaches its minimum value of approximately $1,175,726 near x ≈ 534.5 ft and increases steadily for all larger values of x. Therefore, the least expensive location for point Q is less than 2000 ft from point P.
steps.why: Since C(x) achieves its minimum around x ≈ 535 ft and increases monotonically thereafter, the optimal point Q lies well below 2000 ft from P.
